New Bajaj Pulsar N250SS, Pulsar NS200 Review - More Torque or Sharper Handling?

KS
By Kabir Sharma Indian Automotive & SUV Specialist • via Rushlane.com Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: Rushlane.com Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights
  • Bajaj Auto has slapped its upgrade package on two more Pulsars.
  • We’re talking about the new and upgraded Pulsar NS200 UG and the new and upgraded Pulsar N250 SS.
  • Both these bikes are priced quite close to each other – Pulsar N250 SS at Rs 1.59 lakh and Pulsar NS200 UG at Rs 1.6 lakh (both prices Ex-sh).
⚡ EDITORIAL TAKE • KABIR SHARMA Indian Automotive & SUV Specialist

Bharat NCAP Safety Standards & Indian Road Readiness

In India's rapidly evolving automotive landscape, crashworthiness and real-world durability are driving consumer purchase decisions like never before. As reported by Rushlane.com, indigenous automakers like Tata Motors and Mahindra are setting global safety benchmarks while optimizing suspension and ground clearance for unpredictable road conditions.

Big Picture: Upcoming monthly FADA retail delivery reports and Bharat NCAP rating scorecards will reveal which domestic models capture mass-market dominance.

Bajaj Auto has slapped its upgrade package on two more Pulsars. We’re talking about the new and upgraded Pulsar NS200 UG and the new and upgraded Pulsar N250 SS. Both these bikes are priced quite close to each other – Pulsar N250 SS at Rs 1.59 lakh and Pulsar NS200 UG at Rs 1.6 lakh (both prices Ex-sh).

📌 The Core Development

Looking at just the spec-sheets, Pulsar NS200 UG still comes out as the more tempting option owing to its high-revving liquid-cooled engine and then the more premium perimeter frame along with sportier clip-on handlebar. Also, it costs just Rs 1,000 more than Pulsar N250 SS. However, experience in real world is what matters and that is what we tried to find out at the media rides in Pune.

Where colours are concerned, both these updated Pulsars still don’t get solid colours without graphics. Pulsar N250 SS gets four colours – Brooklyn Black, Pearl Metallic White, Fiery Red Orange and the Atlantic Blue. Only Black and Red get Red painted alloy wheels, while other two colours get Black wheels.

🔍 Background & Sector Context

Shifting the gaze towards Pulsar NS200 UG, we have just three colours and none of them are solid colours and they all get graphics. These include Pearl Metallic White, Ebony Black Racing Red and then the new Nardo Grey. Except for the White colour, which gets Black wheels, the other two get Red painted alloy wheels.

Bajaj Auto has given both these bikes the same upgrade package. So, both of them get the same 5-inch TFT instrument cluster that supports auto brightness, lap timer, document storage, music control and even Google Maps mirroring, which is a cherry on top. This screen is bright and has auto theme switching – Day / Night.

📊 Industry & Real-World Impact

To control this screen, we now get new left-side switchgear which we have seen with other Pulsars. Both Pulsar N250 SS and Pulsar NS200 UG get new right side switchgear too, where Bajaj has added a hazard light button, an integrated engine kill switch / engine starter. The bike now gets a panic brake alert too, which is welcome addition.

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

Upgrade package also involves adjustable clutch and brake levers along with Type-C port. Both bikes now get an electronic throttle body with ride by wire that has enabled Ride Modes. Traction Control with both bikes can be switched off from the screen and then they both get a bi-directional quickshifter too. ABS modes are present with both the bikes and they both get rear radial tyres now.

Apart from the same upgrade package with both Pulsar N250 SS and Pulsar NS200 UG , there are some unique upgrades to these bikes individually too. For example, the Pulsar NS200 UG now gets slightly fatter USD front forks – 37mm, as opposed to 33mm from before. Also, the 199.5cc engine is updated to produce 25 PS and 18.74 Nm. Peak power is up by 1 PS and corresponding RPMs are also slightly higher.
